description: Canonical service_type vocabulary. A service_type names one deployed wire role. This registry is the single source of valid values and per-context eligibility for Service Describe, Realm sync endpoints, Realm join candidates, ServiceRegistrationKey, and the MIMI provider directory. Consumers MUST derive their closed value space from active rows whose valid_in includes the applicable context.
registry_rules: A service_type id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is lowercase snake_case. Only ids present as rows in this registry exist; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

Value spaces are NOT interchangeable. Each row declares valid_in, the set of contexts the id may legally appear in. A service_type valid for Service Describe is not thereby valid as a Realm sync endpoint class or as a ServiceRegistrationKey component. Consumers MUST derive their enum from the rows whose valid_in contains that consumer's context, never from the full row list.

Schema enum values for every service_type selector field MUST be generated from active rows filtered by valid_in; tools/lint_artifacts.py check_service_type_registry asserts each declared JSON pointer.

service_registration_key is the most restrictive context: it admits only service types that are a standalone deployment owning a service DID under a canonical public base. Adding a row to this context means that service type can hold a service identity and appear in ak.root.identity.service_registration.* operations.

The registry is additive. New service types enter as new rows with their own valid_in set; existing wire values never change meaning. Widening an existing row's valid_in is a registry release, not an implementation decision.

service_type is a role name, not a product name. Deployment or implementation identifiers (for example a binary called soland or starid) MUST NOT be registered. A single physical deployment MAY fill more than one role, but each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role. Co-located roles sharing a public binding are selected with GET /_arkret/describe?service_type=<registered-id>; each response advertises only that role's exact supported_operations, profiles, authentication metadata, limits and plaintext visibility. Compound service_type values are forbidden.

This registry governs service_type selector fields only. Adjacent value spaces that happen to use similar words, including the policy source_service_type attribution field, are separate and out of scope.

contexts.description: Top-level service_type of a Service Describe document (schemas/service-describe.schema.json). Every deployable role may describe itself.
Service class of a Realm sync endpoint (schemas/realm.schema.json $defs/sync_endpoint).
Service class permitted to receive join-side submissions (schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json). principal_server is the normal candidate; the others only when Realm policy authorizes them.

The service_type half of a ServiceRegistrationKey (service_type + canonical public_base). Only roles that own a service DID under a public base belong here. Producers and validators MUST reject any service_type absent from this context.

Provider directory descriptor of the MIMI interop surface (schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json $defs/provider_directory). Pinned as a const rather than an enum because the context admits exactly one role.

service_types.description: Account-owning home server: event ingestion, sync, authz projections, key backup, federation. Also acts as an embedded did:webvh host for the identities it serves, which is why it is valid_in service_registration_key both as a subject and as a Service Identity Provider.
OIDC / token issuance and account lifecycle. Hosts no DID documents of its own; obtains its service DID from an external Service Identity Provider.
Standalone did:webvh registry: DID documents, key logs, receipts, watcher/mirror. Self-hosts its own service DID through its local store.
Event sync surface without account authority.
Discovery ingest/query with anti-enumeration and takedown audit.
Long-term archive storage and retrieval surface.
Cryptographic key backup and recovery surface.
MIMI interop provider facade. Deliberately NOT valid_in service_describe: it names a facade role inside the MIMI provider-directory descriptor, not a standalone Arkret service describing itself.
